_about: How written text is said aloud. Years from 1600 to 1999 are said the way people say them (1874 as eighteen seventy-four, 1905 as nineteen oh five, 1900 as nineteen hundred), in English. The screen keeps the written text; these rules only change what the natural voice and the phone voice say. rules: find (a regular expression), say (what to say instead), langs (which languages it applies to). names: how to say a place name the voice gets wrong, as a respelling (for example "Tinbeerwah": "Tin-beer-wah"); used in every language. Changing a rule re-records only the lines it changes. pronounce: the exact way the natural voice says a word, as IPA, sent to Google with every line containing it (the written text never changes); respell is said instead only if Google refuses the pronunciation, and the build then reports it. Use pronounce first; names is for the phone voice or when pronounce cannot be used.

pronounce._help: Ben, 11/10/2026: the voice said Noosa as Nysa. Noosa is said NOO-suh (Australian English), in every language. Google refuses a phrase with an apostrophe (Noosa's), so only the plain words are listed. lang: a language's own IPA (Google checks the sounds against each language and refused the English IPA in de, fr, es, it and ko, and any IPA for Noosa in de, where the respelling Nusa reads the right way) or, with ipa null, only a respelling (Chinese and Japanese need their own spelling systems).
